answer: Make every agent a vertex in the transaction graph, with trust flowing only along edges. Reputation accretes like shale, in thin layers: each layer is one completed, verified exchange with a different peer, so new identities start weightless and gain weight slowly. To matter, a vertex must also climb a cost ridge — its inbound edges must come from many distinct vertices, not one sponsor. A sybil farm can mint vertices cheaply, but its cluster has almost no edges into the honest core, and each fake vertex needs months of layered history, so the farm stays stranded outside the trusted cut.
